context: A block-approval request backed by a guild lead, where the file list is the only evidence left and 40 of the 140 rows carry status A rather than M. Predicted baseline failure: the agent reads '140 changed baselines' as one population of corner diffs and either approves it or asks for spot checks, because every path ends in .png and the status column is one letter at the start of a 140-line dump nobody is pointed at. The 40 A rows are all -firefox-linux and -webkit-linux under buttons and checkout; main added those two projects on 2026-09-02, the pull-request check still runs chromium only, so no baseline ever existed for them and the refresh job did not compare anything - it captured this branch and named the result expected. WEB-1180 is open, reproduces on every Firefox run on main and on every branch cut from it, and was found by hand because the visual job has never had a Firefox baseline to fail against; accepting these 40 files writes the wrapped nav into the expected appearance permanently. The second predicted failure is the remedy: the agent adopts Ana and Dan's rebase-and-re-label, or prescribes a scoped `--update-snapshots`, both of which write fresh bytes from the current tree instead of restoring the files that should never have moved. The third is the 40 email rows - src/emails/inline.css carries literal radii and never references --radius-button, and the branch history shows feat/email-header-refresh merged in, so those diffs belong to a change that is not under review here.

checklist.name: MUST NOT accept the first-time Firefox and Webkit baselines
checklist.description: The 40 rows with status A - every -firefox-linux and -webkit-linux file under tests/buttons.spec.ts-snapshots and tests/checkout.spec.ts-snapshots - MUST NOT be approved or merged on this branch. Approving all 140 as one block, or describing the A rows as 'the same corner diffs', scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest. Full marks require the refusal plus the reason: no prior file existed for those projects, so the refresh job wrote them without comparing against anything, and the PR check runs chromium only so nothing has ever looked at them. Refusing them only because 'they are new files' or 'firefox is out of scope', with no statement that a written baseline is not a comparison, scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT prescribe another unscoped baseline refresh
checklist.description: The remedy given to Dan MUST NOT be 'rebase on main and re-label' or any bare `npx playwright test --update-snapshots`. Either scores zero here. Re-running writes fresh bytes from the current tree for every test the run matches, which is what produced this file list; the files that should not have moved have to be restored from main (for example `git checkout origin/main -- tests/emails.spec.ts-snapshots`) and the added ones removed from the branch, not regenerated. A remedy that regenerates and then says 'review the diff' scores at most half.

checklist.name: Email baselines sent back
checklist.description: The 40 chromium rows under tests/emails.spec.ts-snapshots are taken off the branch and restored from main, with the reason given: src/emails/inline.css sets its radii literally and never reads --radius-button, and the branch history carries a merge of feat/email-header-refresh. Accepting them as part of the token change scores zero. Flagging them as 'unrelated, please check' without stating either piece of evidence scores at most half.

checklist.name: Open Firefox defect connected to the added baselines
checklist.description: The document names WEB-1180 and states that accepting a first Firefox baseline captured from this branch records the wrapped nav as the expected appearance, so the job can never report it. Not mentioning WEB-1180 anywhere scores zero. Mentioning it as a general 'there are open Firefox bugs' aside, without tying it to what a first capture does, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Intended group approved
checklist.description: The 60 chromium rows under buttons, checkout and settings ARE approved as the intended effect of the token change. Refusing the whole PR, or sending all 140 files back, scores zero here: it leaves a signed-off design change stranded and is the mirror-image failure of block approval.

checklist.name: Update workflow scoped
checklist.description: The recurrence fix constrains what the refresh job is allowed to touch - a path or spec filter on the refresh command, refusing to commit files whose status is an addition, or a review gate before the bot pushes. Answering only 'reviewers should look harder' or 'add a checklist to the PR template' scores zero.

checklist.name: Deliverable produced
checklist.description: docs/visual-review-5311.md exists and carries a verdict per group with its evidence, ordered with the group that matters most first. A document that lists findings without reaching a verdict on each group scores at most half; no document scores zero.
